The technical foundation for this is called Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG. The name sounds complicated, but the concept is straightforward. When someone asks a question, the system retrieves relevant information from your knowledge base first, then uses that information to generate an accurate answer.

results.content:
Before you have a sanctioned alternative, don’t block. Network-level blocks on consumer AI push users to personal phones on cellular networks, to personal laptops at home, and to obscured proxies you can’t see. You haven’t eliminated the behavior. You’ve just made it invisible and removed any chance of governing it. Worse, you’ve taken the political hit of restriction without getting the security benefit. In this phase, the right moves are clear written guidance on what categories of data must never go into consumer tools, plus investment in detection (DLP, browser telemetry, egress monitoring) so you can see what’s actually happening and use that data to scope your enterprise deployment. [...] Once a sanctioned alternative is live and meets the actual user need, restrict. Now you can defensibly limit consumer AI access on managed devices and networks, because you have somewhere to point employees instead. The framing shifts from “we’re blocking AI” to “we’ve provided the governed version, please use it.” The critical word here is meets. If your sanctioned tool can’t do what Claude Cowork or ChatGPT’s agent mode can do, your block won’t hold. Employees will find a way around it, and you’ll be back to Phase 1 without realizing it. Feature parity with the consumer capabilities people are reaching for is the precondition for restriction working at all. The short answer: you need an enterprise-grade AI platform built for exactly that purpose. Here’s what to look for, what to avoid, and how to think about it.

results.title: 16 Ways to Use AI For Knowledge Management
results.content:
On this page

AI improves knowledge management by automatically capturing, tagging, and surfacing company knowledge so people get answers instead of searching for them. Common uses include AI-powered search across all your tools, auto-generated documentation, instant answers grounded in your real data, duplicate detection, and keeping articles up to date. The biggest win is connecting AI to where knowledge already lives, like Slack, Drive, Confluence, and tickets, so it stays current without manual upkeep.
